description: We're a team of AI students passionate about technology, creative problem-solving, and building innovative experiences. We combine programming, AI, data analysis, and creative thinking with a strong interest in game development. We're building an engaging astronaut mission simulator that makes space exploration fun and educational.
summary:
SOLSHIFT is an interactive, NASA-data-driven Mars survival and engineering simulator designed to introduce children aged 7–12 to real-world space exploration challenges through hands-on gameplay.

Players take command of Outpost Alpha on Mars, where they must keep three astronauts safe and maintain essential life-support systems until an automated supply ship arrives after 12 Martian days (Sols). Each Sol presents a different engineering emergency, requiring players to solve interactive puzzles involving power distribution, water recycling, radiation shielding, hydroponic agriculture, and autonomous rover operations.

The experience features an illustrated Martian outpost, four real-time resource gauges, a friendly robotic mentor named BOLT, synthesized offline audio, and a merit-based scoring system that rewards genuine mission management rather than effortless progression.

Unlike conventional educational simulations that overwhelm young learners with technical terminology or simplify gameplay into meaningless clicking, SOLSHIFT transforms complex aerospace engineering concepts into intuitive, tactile arcade-style challenges. Its deterministic simulation engine incorporates scientific parameters from NASA's data, allowing players to experience the consequences of their engineering decisions.

The project also demonstrates how real NASA scientific resources can be transformed into accessible educational experiences.
details:
🪐 SOLSHIFT — The Mars Outpost Mission Trainer

🚀 Project Overview & Core Vision

Space exploration is often perceived by youth as distant science fiction or reduced to hyper-dense numerical spreadsheets that alienate learners aged 7 to 12. SOLSHIFT bridges this gap: it translates the rigorous physics of closed-loop Environmental Control and Life Support Systems (ECLSS), photovoltaic dust degradation, and solar radiation into tactile, arcade-style puzzle gameplay.

Players take command of Outpost Alpha at Jezero Crater, Gale Crater, or Meridiani Planum. Across a 12-Sol mission, players must keep three specialized crew members (Zara the Systems Engineer, Leo the Botanist, and Dr. Ana the Flight Surgeon) safe and healthy until an automated supply ship lands.

Key Pillars:

  • Zero Textbook Walls: Information is communicated through visual cues, colorful gauges, comic speech bubbles, and tactile mechanics.
  • Hands-On Action Every Sol: Direct clicking through turns without action is impossible. Advancing from Sol 1 to Sol 12 requires solving dedicated tactile engineering challenges.
  • Earned Ranks, Not Free Medals: The highest honor (Gold Commander) requires genuine operational excellence—building rock shields, maintaining battery health, recycling water, and nourishing hydroponic crops.

🛰️ NASA Space Apps Challenge Alignment

The NASA Operational Challenge is implemented in SOLSHIFT through five interactive, NASA-inspired mission activities designed to simulate the challenges of sustaining human life during deep-space exploration. The Closed-Loop Water Recovery System (WRS) features a realistic 3×3 pipe-rotation puzzle in which players must restore catalytic water flow, alongside an adhesive leak-patching task to preserve 98% of recycled potable water. Photovoltaic Dust Deposition challenges players to solve a solar-wire color-routing puzzle, remove accumulated dust through interactive vent cleaning, and prioritize power-grid recovery using NASA InSight lander dust-deposition data. In Space Radiation Protection (SPE/GCR), players use a Tetris-style regolith-stacking mechanic to construct 50 cm of shielding over crew quarters, demonstrating how protective material can reduce cosmic radiation exposure by 76%. Hydroponic Space Agriculture simulates sustainable food production through interactive watering-can irrigation and LED lighting cycles modeled after NASA's ISS Veggie-01 experiment. Finally, Deep Space Communications Latency introduces realistic communication delays of 4–24 minutes, requiring players to make autonomous decisions and manage emergencies without immediate guidance from Earth.

🔬 Authentic NASA Science & Engineering Datasets

SOLSHIFT's underlying simulation engine is not random; every calculation is derived from published NASA human spaceflight benchmarks:

  1. NASA BVAD (Baseline Values and Assumptions Document):
    • Crew Metabolic Consumption: Oxygen (0.84 kg/crew/sol), Potable Water (2.5 L/crew/sol), Dry Food Ration (0.62 kg/crew/sol).
    • Human Waste Water Loop: 98 closed-loop recovery via catalytic distillation centrifuges.
    • Atmospheric optical depth (τ) dust spikes (analogue to Sol 5 and Sol 14 dust events) reducing solar generation by up to 60.
    • Galactic Cosmic Ray (GCR) background dose (∼0.67 mSv/day) and Solar Particle Event (SPE) proton storm spikes (GLE73 analogue).
    • In-situ Regolith Shielding: Every 10 cm of Martian dirt reduces absorbed dose until 50 cm achieves 76 deflection.
    • Outpost biomass chamber photoperiods (16 h red + blue LED grow lights) producing fresh red romaine lettuce (Lactuca sativa) high in anthocyanin antioxidants.

🎨 7–12 Kid-Friendly UI/UX Philosophy

Following real feedback from kids and teachers, SOLSHIFT rejects cluttered adult dashboards in favor of:

  1. Four Large Visual Gauges:
    • ⚡ Power (0–100%): Tracks battery storage (45 kWh nominal capacity) and solar generation.
    • 💨 Air & Water (0–100%): Tracks oxygen partial pressure and recycled water reserves (300 L starting buffer).
    • 🥗 Food (0–100%): Tracks hydroponic crop maturity and harvest yield.
    • 🛡️ Shield (0–100%): Tracks stacked regolith thickness (0 to 50 cm).
    • Interactive clickable base modules: Solar Array ⚡, Core Hab Dome ⛺, Veggie Greenhouse 🌱, and Regolith Rocks 🪨.
    • The active daily mission module features an animated bouncing ⭐ PLAY! badge so players immediately know what to do without reading blocks of text.
    • An expressive robot buddy who guides the player with single-sentence comic speech bubbles and audio chimes.
    • Optional [📖 NASA Fact] pop-up card for curious students who want to know the real mission history.

🎮 The 12-Sol Operational Curriculum & Mini-Games

The SOLSHIFT mission campaign consists of 12 distinct Martian sols, each introducing a different operational challenge and interactive mini-game.

Sol 1 – Wire Repair & Power tasks players with restoring severed electrical power lines by connecting color-matched red, blue, and yellow terminals.

Sol 2 – Greenhouse Water Pipes focuses on restoring irrigation to dehydrated lettuce through a 3×3 rotating pipe puzzle, followed by an interactive watering-can activity.

Sol 3 – Water Loop Leak Patch challenges players to identify and seal spraying water-pipe leaks by tapping damaged sections and applying silicone adhesive patches.

Sol 4 – Regolith Storm Shelter requires players to protect the crew from cosmic radiation by stacking regolith stone blocks to achieve 50 cm of protective shielding over the habitat bunker.

Sol 5 – Dust Storm & Rescue involves rescuing a rover and securing the base by navigating safe waypoints and adjusting solar panels during a dust storm.

Sol 6 – Rover Motor Fix tests autonomous maintenance skills by having players replace damaged motor-drive gears and perform a test spin without relying on communication with Earth.

Sol 7 – Deep Space Radio Dial introduces communication challenges, requiring players to tune an oscilloscope-style radio slider to the 80° Deep Space Network (DSN) carrier signal while navigating space interference.

Sol 8 – Solar Particle Bunker focuses on life-support maintenance, tasking players with ejecting an overheated, spent CO₂ scrubber core and installing a fresh lithium hydroxide (LiOH) canister.

Sol 9 – Hydroponic Nutrient Boost teaches sustainable crop management through an interactive activity in which players administer mineral nutrient doses to growing lettuce pods.

Sol 10 – Night Battery Triage challenges players to prevent an overnight power blackout by operating physical breaker switches and shedding non-essential loads, such as heavy drilling equipment.

Sol 11 – Blueberry Rock Sample introduces geological exploration, requiring players to collect hematite-rich spherical formations using a robotic magnetic scoop that sweeps across Martian soil.

Sol 12 – First Mars Harvest marks the culmination of the agricultural mission, celebrating the first successful crop harvest through an interactive mini-game in which players catch falling romaine lettuce.

⚙️ Deterministic Simulation Engine & Scoring Physics

SOLSHIFT's core simulation runs on a pure, deterministic engine (SimulationEngine.ts) with mathematical state updates:

Consumables Balance (per Sol):

ΔPotableWater = Generation (WRS + Melt) - (CrewConsumption [2.5 L * 3] + CropIrrigation)

ΔOxygen = MOXIE Production - CrewRespiration [0.84 kg * 3]

ΔBatteryStorage = SolarGeneration(SunHours, DustFactor Tau) - TotalBusDraw(BusA + BusB + BusC + BusD)

AbsorbedDose = (GCR_Background + SPE_SolarStorm) * (1.0 - RegolithShieldPct)

Strict Gold Medal Ranking (No Free Medals):

To eliminate unearned rewards, the scoring engine enforces hard operational gates:

  • Gold Commander 🥇: Requires Composite Score ≥85 pts, Battery ≥40 kWh, Crew Health ≥85, and Active Base Shielding (≥20 cm regolith or active crop cycle).
  • Silver Specialist 🥈: Composite Score ≥70 pts with safe crew arrival.
  • Bronze Survivor 🥉: Composite Score ≥50 pts with base survival.

Technology and Development Tools:

The application was developed using React 18, TypeScript 5.7, Vite 6, and Tailwind CSS. The simulation and scoring engines implement deterministic resource calculations and mission evaluation, while Vitest provides automated testing. The Web Audio API generates interactive sound effects directly in the browser without requiring external audio downloads.

The application requires no user accounts, database, or internet connection during gameplay. Its modular architecture separates interactive mini-games, mission screens, simulation logic, scoring, and audio services. The project currently includes 72 passing automated tests.

Benefits and Intended Impact:

SOLSHIFT makes STEM education more accessible by replacing intimidating technical explanations and passive learning with interactive problem-solving. Children develop an intuitive understanding of resource management, systems engineering, sustainability, scientific reasoning, and autonomous decision-making.

The project also demonstrates how real NASA scientific resources can be transformed into accessible educational experiences. Its offline-first design makes it suitable for schools, classrooms, museums, and planetariums, including environments with limited or unreliable internet access. Its intended long-term impact is to encourage younger generations, particularly those with limited access to advanced STEM resources, to explore science, engineering, and space exploration.

Creativity and Design Considerations:

SOLSHIFT's central creative approach is turning complex aerospace engineering into tactile, arcade-style activities without sacrificing the underlying scientific concepts. Instead of presenting children with equations and telemetry tables, it allows them to physically interact with simulated systems through puzzles, visual feedback, and immediate consequences.

A friendly robot mentor, BOLT, provides short guidance messages and optional NASA fact cards for deeper exploration. Four large visual gauges communicate the status of power, air and water, food, and radiation shielding without overwhelming young players.

During development, key considerations included scientific grounding, age-appropriate interaction, accessibility, meaningful learning, realistic resource trade-offs, intuitive navigation, and offline compatibility. The scoring system was also designed to prevent unearned rewards, ensuring that successful missions reflect genuine operational decisions rather than simple progression.

SOLSHIFT ultimately aims to make every Sol a learning experience, allowing children to discover that surviving on Mars requires creativity, engineering, teamwork, and responsible management of limited resources.
